source.snippet: Many users have access to local hardware capable of running smaller models efficiently, while still relying on larger cloud models for reasoning-intensive tasks. Today, applications typically have to build their own orchestration layer to decide which tasks should run locally vs. which should run in the cloud. (Feature request, 2026-06-22)

problem_statement: Developers building AI applications must hand-roll orchestration logic to route inference tasks between local models and cloud LLMs, leading to duplicated effort and brittle per-app solutions with no standardized layer.
target_segment: AI application developers and small ML engineering teams using Ollama or similar local inference runtimes who also use cloud LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).
notes: Single GitHub feature request — weak solo signal, but the underlying need is corroborated by broader market trends (LiteLLM, RouteLLM). Buyer context: developers at companies spending on cloud LLM APIs who want to reduce cost by offloading to local hardware. A managed routing proxy (SaaS or SDK) with smart task classification could sell at $50–200/mo to cost-conscious teams. Signal strength kept at 2 due to single source.
